# The names

Where neon1, its slogan and its products get their names.

## neon1

The name nods to Neo from *The Matrix*, who brought peace between man and machine. Neo means new, and neon is unmissable. It's always written with a lowercase n.

## "1 is glad to be of service."

The slogan nods to Robin Williams' Andrew from *Bicentennial Man*, a machine who spends two centuries being of service while searching for his humanity. The 1 is me, Pradeep, neon1's sole owner and your dedicated deputy.

## The legal names

- **neon1 LLC**, a New York limited liability company, does business as **neon1**, a registered assumed name (see the [state registration](registration.md)).
- **N1 Supply LLC** does business as **N1 Supply**. It is an affiliate of neon1 LLC.

## Product names

Repositories that neon1 builds mainly for its own use carry the `neon1-` prefix, such as neon1-site and neon1-corpus. Products made for the public or for clients get names of their own, such as [Ready, Secure, Go](../products/ready-secure-go.md).

## What to expect

- **Where:** remote across the US, or on site within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. Outside the US, ask.
- **When:** Monday to Thursday 6pm to 9pm, Friday 6pm to 8pm, and weekends 8am to 8pm, Eastern time.
- **Size:** a week or two up to six weeks, with a few clients at a time, so each gets my full attention.
- **First call:** free and 15 minutes, about your needs. Options come afterward, in writing.
- **Before the call, if you like:** write your project down in a [free 1NEON account](../guides/free-accounts.md) and ask for a free assessment of it. I read it before we talk.
- **After:** a short proposal with one recommendation, or options when there's a real choice. Nothing starts until you approve it.

## Availability and urgent issues

I work in planned appointments on weekday evenings and weekends. There's no 24/7 or emergency response. If something can't wait, such as a security incident in progress, an outage, or fraud on an account, contact a provider with emergency coverage, and your bank or the service involved, first. Ongoing care after a project, with any response times, is agreed in writing before it starts.

## Report a bug

Something broken on neon1.tech, 1NEON, or Neo? [Report a bug](https://neon1.tech/report-bug/) says where it happened and what happened, with an optional email and screenshots. Don't include passwords, health details, or payment information.

Leave passwords, health details, and payment information out of any first message.

# How a project runs

Listen, propose, decide, build and hand over.

1. **Listen.** The goal, the systems and people involved, the constraints, and who will own the result. It starts with a free 15-minute call about your needs, and I read anything you've written in a free 1NEON account before we talk.
2. **Propose.** A recommendation, or options when there's a real choice, each with scope, acceptance criteria, cost to build and run, and alternatives considered.
3. **Decide.** You approve the scope and price. Sometimes the answer is a setting, an existing product, or leaving things as they are.
4. **Build.** Reviewable changes, tested against the acceptance criteria, including failure and rollback. Scope changes need your approval.
5. **Hand over.** Evidence that it meets the criteria, documentation, and a walkthrough for whoever runs it. Ongoing care is optional.

[See how it works](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live): a guided walkthrough of a fictional project in 1NEON.

# Service agreement

neon1's service agreement, as a client organization signs it once in 1NEON: how work is agreed, purchases, paying, ownership, confidentiality, records, quality, limits, and ending.

**The short version**

- One agreement covers every project. Each option you approve sets that project's scope, price, and timeline.
- A price is fixed, or an estimate billed by the hour that never passes its high end without your approval. Invoices are due in 15 days.
- An admin signs once in 1NEON. Either of us can end it with 14 days' notice.

Edition 2.0

This agreement is between neon1 LLC, doing business as neon1 ("neon1", "I", "me"), and the organization named where it is signed in 1NEON ("you"). It covers every project I do for you while it is in effect.

## How work is agreed

Each project has a proposal in 1NEON, issued in numbered revisions. When your decision maker approves an option, its ID (for example 0039-r2-B) fixes that project's scope, price, and timeline. A change is agreed the same way, by approving an option in the next revision. This agreement governs everything else, and if a proposal and this agreement disagree, this agreement wins.

## Purchases

Prices for equipment, software, and services from other vendors are estimates. You buy them yourself, unless an approval says that I buy them for you. When I do, you pay me back exactly what I paid, shown by the receipt in 1NEON, with no markup.

## Paying

I send invoices through 1NEON. Each one is due within 15 days unless it says otherwise. An option's price is either fixed or an estimate, and the proposal says which. A fixed price is the whole price for the work described. An estimate is billed for the hours I work, at the rate it states; each hour is listed in 1NEON, and the total never passes the estimate's high end unless you approve a change first. An option may ask for a deposit when it is approved, as the proposal states. A deposit counts toward the final invoice; if the work done comes to less than a deposit you paid, I refund the difference. You can pay by bank transfer (ACH), card, check, Zelle, or wire. If an invoice is more than 30 days overdue, I may pause work until it is paid, after telling you.

## What you provide

You give me timely answers, the access the work needs, and accounts held in your organization's name. Please don't put passwords or other secrets in 1NEON.

## Ownership

Once you have paid for a project, what I made for you in it is yours. I keep my general know-how and the tools I had before or build for my own use, and open-source software stays under its own license.

## Confidentiality

We each keep what we learn about the other's business private, and use it only for the work. This doesn't cover what is already public or what the law requires us to disclose.

## Regulated data

I don't handle health records, payment card data, or similar regulated personal data unless we sign a separate agreement for it first, such as a business associate agreement.

## Records

I keep project records, signed approvals, invoices, and receipts, and I don't delete them on a schedule. If you ask me to delete something, I will, except what the law requires me to keep.

## Quality

I do the work with care. If something I delivered doesn't work as agreed and you tell me within 30 days of handover, I fix it at no charge.

## Limits

My total liability for any claim is limited to what you paid me for that project in the 12 months before the claim. Neither of us is liable to the other for indirect or consequential losses, such as lost profits.

## Ending

Either of us may end this agreement with 14 days' written notice, by message in 1NEON or by email. You pay for the work done and the purchases made up to that point.

## Signing and law

We agree to sign and keep these records electronically, and a name typed in 1NEON is a signature. You can ask me for a paper copy at any time. New York law governs this agreement.

# 1NEON help

Short answers about using the 1NEON client portal.

Signed in? Tap **?** at the top right of any page for help with that page.

## Getting started

### What is 1NEON?
The portal where we run your projects together: what you need, the work, the results, and the handover. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### Can I try it first?
Yes, with no account. The [guided walkthrough](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) takes about three minutes and plays a made-up project on the real portal, and the full story takes about 17 minutes. The [sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) is one made-up project to read. The [interactive demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/) is a working copy where you pick who to be, and changes stay in your browser until **Start over**. [From free account to client](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free) follows one free account from sign-up to client. Short walkthroughs show one thing: [joining from an invitation](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite), [adding a passkey](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey), [adding an authenticator app](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator), and [texts and text codes](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### How do I get in?
Start a free account from **Start for free** on the sign-in screen, or open the link in an invite email from neon1 or your organization. Sign in with a code sent to your email, or with a passkey. No password needed. Watch [starting a free account](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=free) or [joining from an invite](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite). [Free 1NEON accounts](https://neon1.tech/knowledge/guides/free-accounts/) says what it holds.

### I didn't get the sign-in code.
Check spam or promotions, wait a minute, and choose **Send a new code**. Codes work for a few minutes, in the browser that asked. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

### Is there a tour?
Yes, at your first sign-in. Replay it from **?** or your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=invite).

## Projects and the four layers

### What are Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize?
The four layers of every project. **Needs** is what you want and the options, **Execute** the work, **Observe** the results against the goals, and **Normalize** the handover, training, and care. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live).

### What should I do first on a project?
Look at **Next step** at the top. It says what has to happen now and who it's waiting on. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### What do Not assessed, On track, At risk, and Off track mean?
They're the project's health, as the team assesses it. A new project is **Not assessed** until the team sets it, and moving stages doesn't change it. Items have their own status: To do, In progress, Blocked, or Done. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we rename, reorder, or hide stages?
Projects follow the new names and order. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it. Decide still asks for an approved option, and Closed still ends a project.

### How do I tell you what I need?
On the **Needs** tab, tap **Add request** and finish a sentence with a few taps. Only the first choice is required. **Define another need** adds more. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=needs).

### Do I have to write a lot?
No. Each section shows an example and one-tap suggestions, and a short answer is enough. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### How do I know when something changes?
The bell glows. Tap it to see what and who. Important changes also email you, and you choose which under **Notifications** in your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### How do I comment or change an item?
Tap its title to open its status, owner, due date, details, and comments, which your whole organization sees. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### How do I check something off?
Tick the box beside it. A choice between options counts once one is approved, and a measure at its target. Status updates, decisions, and uploaded files don't count, but a **File needed** does, ticked when you send it. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover).

### How do I delete something?
Use the trash button or **Delete** in its panel, and confirm. Approved options and decisions can't be deleted, since they record what was agreed. Files can be deleted by their uploader and admins.

### What does the onion next to a project mean?
Progress. Needs is the center ring and Normalize the outside, each filling as work gets done.

### What does the board show?
Every project as a card in its stage. Drag a card to move it, or use **Move to** on a phone. Move a closed project back the same way, or choose **Reopen**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What does the timeline show?
Under **Projects**, **Timeline** draws each project from start to target date, colored by layer. The dashed line is today, the diamond the target, and red stripes time past the target. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=care).

### How do I start a project?
Choose **New project** and answer a few questions. It starts with a checklist you can change later. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=start).

### Is there a simpler way for a small job?
Yes. For a fix of a few hours, neon1 starts a **Quick fix** with no proposal. neon1 sends one quote, a fixed price or hours at a rate capped at the most hours quoted, and nothing is paid up front. **Next step** says **Approve the quote**, and you sign once. When it's fixed, you accept that one step with your signature, and neon1 sends one invoice. Your organization still signs neon1's service agreement once before its first approval.

### What is the calendar on Home?
Due dates, milestones, project targets, and your organization's events, a month at a time. Choose a day to see them. Editors add leave, closures, meetings, or care plan dates, one-off or repeating. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=calendar).

### What is Insights?
Charts from your organization's data, such as open and overdue work, on-time finishes, and days to a decision. The page explains each number. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=observe).

## Proposals, decisions, and signing

### What is a proposal revision?
neon1's options are issued together as a numbered proposal, such as 0039-r1, each option with its own ID, such as 0039-r1-B. Issuing freezes a copy, so what you approve is what you read. Changed options come in the next revision (0039-r2), and earlier ones stay readable, marked as replaced. Past a revision's price recheck date, approval waits for a refresh. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

### How do I approve an option?
On **Needs**, compare the options and choose **Approve this option**. Add any conditions, type your full name, and tick the box. Your typed name is your signature. The approval records the option's terms as shown (ID, description, price and whether it's fixed or an estimate, hours, rate, timeline, outside costs, and purchases) with your name and the time. To ask for a change, comment on the option or send a marked-up proposal. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I download the proposal?
Yes. **Read the proposal**, under the options, puts everything on one page. **Print or save as PDF** keeps a copy, and **Download Word** gives one to mark up. Each page carries the number, such as 0039-r1. Approving in 1NEON counts the same as signing on paper. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### How do I suggest changes to a proposal?
Comment on an option, or mark up the Word download and upload it to **Files**. When 1NEON asks "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?", choose **Yes**. neon1 answers with the next revision. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Who buys equipment or software for a project?
You do, in your organization's name, unless you agree neon1 does. Expected purchases appear under **Purchases** in Execute once you approve. Mark each bought and **Attach the receipt**. neon1 buys only with the decision maker's signature or initials, and is paid back at cost, with the receipt. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if we need something new after approving?
Add it as a request. If it changes the agreed scope, it waits for the next revision with its own price, so no work or cost is added without a written change.

### Who can approve?
The project's named decision maker, or, if none, an admin of your organization. Only an admin can name or change the decision maker, under **People** on the overview. Each change is recorded. neon1 can't be named, except in its own organization. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Can I change my mind after approving an option?
Yes, until you accept the handover. The decision maker presses **Choose this instead** on another option, says why, and signs again. Nothing is billed twice. What was invoiced for the earlier option counts toward the new one, hours already worked count toward its hours, and any overpayment comes back as a credit at handover. The earlier decision stays on record, marked replaced, with your reason on the new one. To return to a replaced option, neon1 confirms it in the next revision with today's prices. If none of the options fits the change, ask neon1 for a new one. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### What does approving an option commit us to?
That your organization agreed to the option as shown: its scope, cost, timeline, and conditions. Both sides can rely on it, alongside your signed agreement with neon1, which governs the paid work.

### How do I accept a handover step?
On **Normalize**, steps are ticked as they're done. Once all are, the decision maker chooses **Accept the handover** and signs with their typed name. One signature accepts every step. **Check it and accept** accepts one step early. Accepted steps can't be edited, and acceptance prompts the final invoice. Watch [the handover](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=handover) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final).

### What do Cost, Quality, and Effort mean?
neon1's 1 to 5 rating of each option, where more dots is always better. **Cost** is the total cost, **Quality** how fully it meets your requirements, and **Effort** your team's effort to adopt and run it. **How this adds up** shows the hours and when you'd pay. Demo and walkthrough figures are illustrative. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=propose).

## Files

### How do I send a file?
Use **Upload** next to a file I asked for, or upload in **Files**. Files filed at **Organization level** belong to your whole organization. Choose a project to file under it, in one of its layers or at **Project level** for the project as a whole. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=listen).

### Can I move a file later?
Yes. Choose **Move** on a file, and pick Organization level, a project, or a layer of a project. The file itself isn't touched, only where it's listed.

### Are files safe?
Every file is virus-checked before anyone can download it and stays private to your organization.

### What can I upload?
Any file up to 100 MB. Don't upload passwords, keys, or other secrets, malware, or regulated data such as health or payment card details unless we have a written agreement that covers it.

## People and access

### What can viewers, editors, and admins do?
Viewers read and comment. Editors also add and change work. Admins also invite people and change access and settings. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### How do I invite someone?
Admins choose **Invite people** on **People**, and the person gets an email link. If it didn't go out or got lost, choose **Resend**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=team).

### Can 1NEON text me?
Once texts are on. Add your mobile number on your profile, agree to texts, save, and type the code 1NEON texts you. Texts only say something new is waiting, with a link, and never name your organization, projects, or files. Reply STOP to turn them off. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=texts).

### Why does it ask me to confirm it's me?
Admin actions (inviting people, changing access or settings, and deleting a project or someone else's comment or file) also need a recent confirmation with a passkey, an authenticator app, or a text-message code. That way a stolen email account isn't enough. Add one under Two-step verification on your profile, and a second is a backup. You won't be asked again for 12 hours in that sign-in. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

### Can I use an authenticator app?
Yes. On your profile, choose **Set up** next to Authenticator app, scan the code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, or similar, and type the 6-digit code. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=authenticator).

### What's a passkey?
A sign-in with your face, fingerprint, or device PIN instead of a code. It's phishing-resistant, since it only works on the real 1NEON site. Add one under Two-step verification on your profile. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=passkey).

## Your account

### How do I change my name or the look?
Open your profile from the menu, change your name, title, theme, menu, or notifications, and choose **Save**. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=profile).

### How do I sign out?
Open your profile and choose **Sign out**.

### I lost my phone or my authenticator app.
You can still sign in with an emailed code. The second step is only for admin actions. If you have another method, confirm with it, then remove the lost one and add a new one. If you've lost every method, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) from your account's address. Email alone isn't enough, since a stolen mailbox is what the second step guards against. I confirm who you are by calling a number already on record (never one from the email), plus another admin's written OK if your organization has one. Then I remove the lost methods, record it, and email you. Only admin actions wait meanwhile. There's no self-service reset.

### My email address changed.
Your email is how 1NEON knows you, so you can't change it on your profile. Ask an admin to invite the new address and deactivate the old one, or email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech). Earlier work stays under the old address.

### Who do I ask for access?
An admin of your organization. If you don't know who that is, or neon1's access needs to change, email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

## Invoices and paying

### Is a price fixed or an estimate?
The option says which, and **How this adds up** shows the work behind it. A fixed price is the whole price for the work described, changed only by a change you approve. An estimate is a range of hours at the option's hourly rate. You pay for hours worked, each listed as logged, never past the high end without your approval. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

### Where do I see the hours worked?
In **Hours**, under Execute. Each entry has its date, what it went to, and its length in quarter hours. Billed hours carry the invoice's number. On a fixed price, hours are a record, not a bill. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=build).

### What if the work needs more hours than the estimate?
The high end is the most you pay for the approved work. Hours past it are listed, not billed. If the work itself must change, neon1 says so before the high end and issues a revision with the new price, and nothing is added until you approve. If the work takes less than the deposit covered, neon1 refunds the difference as a credit.

### Where are invoices and payments?
In **Invoices**, under Execute, with what's paid and left on each. Each opens on neon1's letterhead with its number, lines, due date, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### How do I pay an invoice?
Choose **Pay**. Stripe's hosted page opens for bank transfer (ACH, preferred) or card, and 1NEON never sees your details. A card shows as paid within a minute. A bank transfer shows as started that day and paid once it clears, usually in a few business days. Check, Zelle, or wire work too, with the invoice number in the memo, and neon1 records them on arrival. [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay).

### What if my bank payment doesn't go through?
No money moved. The invoice reopens with the failed payment listed, and 1NEON tells you and neon1 that day. Choose **Pay again** or another way to pay. Nothing is added to what you owe.

### Do I get a receipt?
The invoice is your receipt. Once paid it reads **Paid in full**, with each payment's date, amount, and method, and prints or saves as a PDF. Billing contacts are also emailed when a payment arrives.

### Is there a fee for paying by card, or for paying late?
No. The total is what you pay, however you pay, with no card surcharge, late fee, or interest. A late invoice shows as overdue, and neon1 may pause work, after telling you, once one is more than 30 days overdue.

### What if I think an invoice is wrong?
Say so before you pay. Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with the invoice number and line. neon1 fixes it with a credit, or voids it with a reason and issues a new one, on the record.

### When are invoices sent?
As your option's **When you pay** says. A deposit, half a fixed price or half an estimate's low end, comes at approval. The rest comes at handover acceptance: the remainder of a fixed price, or the hours worked less the deposit. Purchases are billed at cost with the receipt, and care plans monthly. Invoices are due in 15 days unless the option says otherwise, and each emails your billing contacts. Watch [the deposit](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=pay) and [the final invoice](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=final).

### Can an invoice be changed?
Not once issued. A mistake is fixed with a credit, or by voiding it with a reason, both on record. An invoice with a payment, or one clearing, can't be voided.

### What is the service agreement?
neon1's terms for all work with your organization: how work is agreed, paying, ownership, confidentiality, and ending it. An admin signs it once in 1NEON, from **Settings**, before the first approval. Read it any time at [/1NEON/agreement](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/agreement). [Watch it](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live?play=decide).

## Support and your data

### Something urgent is wrong. Who do I tell?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech) with what happened and when. neon1 works planned hours with no emergency response, so for something that can't wait, such as bank fraud or an outage, contact the provider responsible first. Report a security problem in the portal itself to [security@neon1.tech](mailto:security@neon1.tech).

### Can we get a copy of our data?
Yes, any time, without asking me. An admin opens **Settings** and chooses **Download everything** under Your data. You get one zip with every project's records, decisions and signatures, proposals, invoices, payments, and handover steps as JSON and CSV, plus every comment, the activity history, every uploaded file as uploaded, and projects in Trash. README.txt says what each file holds, and manifest.json lists every file with a SHA-256 checksum. Not included: unissued invoice drafts, files still uploading, and each person's notifications, sign-in methods, and display preferences. If anything is missing, the file ends in -partial.zip instead of -complete.zip, and the README and Settings say what and why.

### What happens to our data when the work ends?
It's kept as the record of our work unless your organization asks me to delete it. Your organization can stop using 1NEON any time and download everything from Settings first. The [privacy policy](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/privacy) has the details, including how long backups and audit records last.

### Who can I contact?
Email [hello@neon1.tech](mailto:hello@neon1.tech).

# Working with neon1

Short answers on where, when, how long, cost, and how data is handled.

## Do you come on site?

Yes, within about 30 miles of Queens, NY. Otherwise I work remotely across the US, or on your network through a connection I remove when the job's done. Outside the US, ask.

## When do you work?

Monday to Thursday 6pm to 9pm, Friday 6pm to 8pm, and weekends 8am to 8pm, Eastern. The booking calendar shows what's open.

## Can I start without a call?

Yes. [Start a free 1NEON account](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/?signup=1) and write down what you need, on your own time. When it's ready, ask for a free assessment and book the 15-minute call. I read your project before we talk.

[Free 1NEON accounts](https://neon1.tech/knowledge/guides/free-accounts/) has the details.

## How do you treat our data and accounts?

I use only the access the job needs, keep your information confidential, and remove my access when we're done. We sign a short [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md) once, before any paid work.

Each project is then a [proposal](../examples/proposal.md): one recommendation, or options when there's a real choice. What you approve is what we both agree to. Personal or health data needs the right agreement first, such as a Business Associate Agreement.

## What if something urgent comes up?

I work in planned appointments, with no 24/7 or emergency response. An incident in progress or an outage needs a provider with emergency coverage first.

For anything your business can't go a day without, I take the work only when someone on your side runs it day to day, and the handover is written for that person. A care plan sets my response times in writing, within my working hours.

## How long does a project take?

It depends on the scope, so the proposal gives the schedule. Larger projects run in phases you approve one at a time. I take a few clients at a time, so each gets my full attention.

## How is the cost worked out?

After we talk, I send a short proposal: one recommendation, or options when there's a real choice, each with what it covers, its upkeep, and its cost. You approve it, and the cost changes only if you approve a change.

Every option has the same security baseline: multi-factor sign-in, the least access the job needs, encryption that fits the data, a tested restore, and a way back from every big change. A smaller option does less, not worse. See [how I price my work](../engagement/pricing.md).

## How do invoices work?

Invoices come through [1NEON](../products/1neon.md), in the project they belong to, and are due within 15 days. You can pay by bank transfer or card online, or by check, Zelle, or wire, with no surcharge.

A project usually starts with a deposit, and the rest is billed when you accept the handover. An estimate bills only the hours worked, and never passes its high end without your approval. Anything I buy for you is paid back at cost, with no markup.

## Do you run security training?

I run informational security awareness sessions for groups, from parents and teachers to engineers and executives: phishing, fraud, passwords, networks, and cameras. They're practical, not certified training. For controls, evidence, and audit preparation, see [security readiness](../guides/use-case-security-readiness.md).

## What don't you do?

I don't repair electronics, do licensed electrical or alarm work, issue audit opinions, give legal advice, or handle personal or health data before the right agreements and insurance are in place. I can help you get those agreements.

# 1NEON

The neon1 client portal that comes with a client engagement, where each project runs from the first call to handover.

The neon1 client portal at [neon1.tech/1NEON](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/). Each project runs through four layers: Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize. Proposals, signed decisions, files, invoices, and results stay together from first call to handover.

- **Available now,** as part of working with neon1. It comes with a client engagement and isn't sold on its own.
- **Who it helps:** the people at a client organization who follow a project, send files, and approve options, and the administrators who decide who can see what.
- **For example,** I issue a proposal numbered 0039-r1 with two options. The decision maker compares them and signs approval of 0039-r1-B with a typed name. 1NEON keeps the signature, the time, and a copy of the option's terms as they saw them. The deposit invoice follows in the same project, payable by bank transfer or card.

## Current limits

- Access is by invitation, from neon1 or an administrator of your organization, or through a free, limited account you make yourself to share your needs before we work together.
- Online payments go through Stripe Checkout, by bank transfer (ACH) or card. Checks, Zelle, and wires are recorded by hand when they arrive.
- An admin can download everything at any time, from Settings: every project's records, decisions, signatures, invoices, and payments as JSON and CSV, plus every comment, the activity history, projects in Trash, and every file as uploaded, with a manifest.json listing what's included or left out. The zip's name ends in -complete or -partial.
- Text messages work only once they're switched on and you've agreed to them on your profile.

## Next step

[See how it works](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/live) in a guided walkthrough of a fictional project, about three minutes. You can also read a [sample project](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/example) or [try the demo](https://neon1.tech/1NEON/demo/), which runs in your browser with made-up data. To use 1NEON for real, start with [a first call](../engagement/contact.md). For help inside the portal, see [1NEON help](../faq/1neon-help.md).

# 1NEON guide: overview, names, and addresses

What 1NEON is, how its frame works, every kind of ID and name it shows, and the address of every page.

1NEON is neon1's client portal at neon1.tech/1NEON. Each client organization runs its projects there with neon1. Every project moves through four layers, N E O N: **Needs** (what's wanted, and the options), **Execute** (the work), **Observe** (results checked against the goals), and **Normalize** (handover, training, and care). This guide covers every page, state, and action, so Neo can explain, link, tour, and plan any action.

## Who's who

- **neon1** is the *operator*: it proposes options, does the work, and can enter every client organization. The operator role comes from sign-in configuration, never from portal data.
- **A client organization** (also an organization, a client, or a tenant) is one business or household neon1 works with. Its admins or neon1 invite its people.
- **neon1's own organization** has the slug `neon1` and the client ID **N1-0001**. There neon1 is also the client, so its people may approve options and name decision makers, which they can't do in any other organization.
- **A member** is a person in an organization, with one access level there: viewer, editor, or admin. One person can belong to several organizations with a different level in each.

## IDs and names people see

| Looks like | What it is | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `N1-0001`, `N1-0002` | An organization's **client ID**, numbered in the order clients joined. N1-0001 is neon1 itself. | Chooser, All clients, organization header |
| `acme-dental` | An organization's **slug**, its handle in addresses | `/1NEON/o/acme-dental/...` |
| `FLOW-1`, `MIG-2`, `HOME-1`, `PRJ-3` | A **project key**: a prefix from the project's template plus a number counted per organization and prefix | Cards, lists, the project page, search |
| `0039`, `0039-r2` | A **proposal number** and one of its **revisions**. Each project has one proposal; the first 1NEON issued is 0039, and each change is issued as the next revision | The proposal strip under Options, the proposal page, its PDF and Word copies |
| `0039-r2-B` | An **option ID**: the revision and the option's letter. A decision names the ID it approved | Options, decisions, purchases bought for an option |
| `INV-0039-01` | An **invoice number**: the proposal's number (or the project key when there's no proposal) and the invoice's place in the project. Set when neon1 issues it | Invoices, the invoice page, card statements (`NEON1* INV003901`) |
| Item titles | Items (requests, tasks, options, measures, and so on) are shown by title; their IDs only appear in links (`#item-…`) | Inside a project |

Key prefixes come from the New project template: Blank is `PRJ`, Cloud migration `MIG`, Workflow automation `FLOW`, AI assistant `AI`, Security readiness `SEC`, and Personal or home tech `HOME`. The number counts up per prefix within one organization, so `MIG-1` in two organizations are two projects.

## The frame around every signed-in page

- **Menu** (top left; **Menu** at the bottom on phones) opens every page: Home, Board, Projects, Files, Insights, People, Settings, the four layers, and your profile. Choosing **Mini** on the profile also keeps a slim column of icons on the left.
- **Organization chooser** at the top of the menu switches between organizations a person belongs to. neon1 also sees **All clients** there.
- **Search** (the search button, Ctrl K or ⌘K, or `/`) jumps to any page or project and starts common actions: Start a new project and Upload a file for editors and admins, Invite people for admins.
- **?** (top right) opens help for the page in view: what it's for, a few how-tos, **Show me on this page** (a spotlight tour of that page), and **Full tour**.
- **The bell** glows when something new happened in the organization: a file upload, a decision, a stage move, a new comment, and similar. Opening it lists what changed and who did it.
- **Neo** sits at the bottom right: the assistant that answers questions, links to pages, runs tours, and, with the person's go-ahead, does things for them.
- **A read-only banner** shows on All clients: "read only. Open a client to make changes."

## Themes

Matrix offers **Awake** (light, the default) and **Plugged** (dark). Sentinel offers **Providence** (light) and **Desert of the real** (dark). The landing theme switch changes the family without changing the mode. Profile choices use the same names; **Match my device** follows the device setting within the chosen family. Neo's window follows the page.

## Addresses

Signed-in pages live under `https://neon1.tech/1NEON/`. `{org}` is the organization's slug and `{KEY}` a project key.

| Page | Address |
|---|---|
| Sign-in | `/1NEON/` |
| Home (the organization's starting page) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace` |
| Board | `/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow` |
| Projects (list and timeline) | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects` |
| New project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new` |
| One project, Overview | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}` |
| One project, a layer | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, or `/normalize` |
| Options on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#options` |
| The project's proposal | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal` |
| A project's invoices | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/execute#billing` |
| One invoice | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{invoiceId}` |
| The service agreement, to sign | `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` |
| Files asked for on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/needs#files` |
| One item on a project | `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/{layer}#item-{itemId}` |
| One layer across all projects | `/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/needs` (also `execute`, `observe`, `normalize`) |
| People | `/1NEON/o/{org}/people` |
| Files | `/1NEON/o/{org}/documents` |
| Insights | `/1NEON/o/{org}/insights` |
| Settings | `/1NEON/o/{org}/settings` |
| Your profile | `/1NEON/me` (two-step verification at `/1NEON/me#security`) |
| All clients (neon1 only) | `/1NEON/all/workflow` |
| FAQs, public | `/1NEON/faqs` |
| Guided walkthrough, public, the way in | `/1NEON/live` (whole story: `?play=full`; short ones: `?play=free`, `invite`, `passkey`, `authenticator`, `texts`, `calendar`; one chapter: `?play=signin`, `profile`, `team`, `start`, `needs`, `listen`, `propose`, `decide`, `pay`, `build`, `change`, `observe`, `handover`, `final`, `care`; client: `&scenario=harborline`, `quillwork`, or `fenwick`) |
| Sample project, public | `/1NEON/example` (`?scenario=harborline`, `quillwork`, or `fenwick`) |
| Interactive demo, public | `/1NEON/demo/` |
| Privacy, terms, cookies, service agreement | `/1NEON/privacy`, `/1NEON/terms`, `/1NEON/cookies`, `/1NEON/agreement` |

The address word for Execute is `execute` and for Normalize is `normalize`. Older links that say `execution` or `next` still work.

## Spotlight anchors

Tours point at named spots, which exist only on the page listed and only while on screen.

| Anchor | Page | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `nav-home`, `nav-board`, `nav-projects`, `nav-layers`, `nav-files`, `nav-me` | Every page | Menu entries (the menu must be open, or Mini on) |
| `menu` | Every page | The menu button |
| `search` | Every page | The search button |
| `help` | Every page | The ? button |
| `notifications` | Organization pages | The bell |
| `needs-you`, `coming-up`, `get-started`, `activity` | Home | Needs you, Coming up, Get started, Recent activity |
| `board-column`, `board-card` | Board, All clients | A stage column, a project card |
| `new-project`, `project-list` | Projects | New project button, the list |
| `next-step`, `stage`, `layers` | One project | Next step box, the stage line, the layer tabs |
| `proposal` | One project, Needs | The proposal strip under Options: the revision, its price check, and Issue or Read the proposal |
| `wizard` | New project | The questions |
| `layer-list` | One layer across projects | The list |
| `invite`, `people-list` | People | Invite people, the list of people |
| `upload` | Files | The upload area |
| `kpis`, `weekly`, `by-layer` | Insights | The numbers on top, Finished per week, Projects by layer |
| `stages` | Settings | The stage rows |
| `passkey` | Profile | Two-step verification |

# 1NEON guide: projects, stages, layers, and items

How a project moves through stages and the four layers, every kind of item and its states, Next step, health, the proposal and its revisions, signed approvals, fixed prices and estimates, hours, purchases, handover acceptance, invoices, and payments.

## A project

A project is one piece of work for one organization. It has a key (such as `FLOW-1`), a name, a short summary, an outcome ("what will be true when it's done"), a target date, a stage, a health, the people on it with their roles, sensitive-data flags (PII, PHI, or payment data), and items in four layers. Every change records who and when. Every edit carries the version last seen, so two people can't silently overwrite each other: the later save is shown what changed and asked to choose.

A project can be **archived** (kept, read only, off the main lists; **Restore from archive** brings it back) or moved to **Trash** by an admin, who types the project's key to confirm. A trashed project leaves every view but is kept, and erased only if the client asks.

## Stages and the board

An organization's workflow is a row of stages, each tied to one layer. The default stages, in order:

| Stage | Layer | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| Intake | Needs | Fit call held |
| Listen | Needs | Discovery complete, baseline metrics recorded |
| Propose | Needs | Options published to the client |
| Decide | Needs | An option approved |
| Build | Execute | All milestone tasks done (limit: 3 projects at once) |
| Verify | Observe | Checks pass, after metrics recorded |
| Hand over | Normalize | Handover accepted |
| Care | Normalize | Ongoing care, or closed |
| Closed | Normalize | (the end) |

The **Board** shows each project as a card (key, name, health, time in stage) in its stage's column, under the "Done when" line and count. Editors and admins drag cards, or use **Move to** on a phone. In **Settings**, admins rename, reorder, limit, and hide stages and edit "Done when", confirming it's them to save. A hidden stage still shows while a project is in it.

Two stages keep their roles under any name or position: **Decide** is the gate (moving past it without an approved option asks for a reason, which is recorded), and **Closed** ends a project. **Reopen**, or dragging it back, moves a closed project to the stage before. Moving backward never asks for a reason, and moving never changes health.

**All clients** (neon1 only) is the same board across every organization, read only, grouped by organization or as one board.

## The four layers and their items

A project page has tabs for **Overview** and each layer, which groups its items by kind. The onion beside the name has a ring per layer, Needs in the center, each filling as work gets done.

| Kind | Layer | What it is | Statuses |
|---|---|---|---|
| Request | Needs | Something the client wants, built as a sentence of taps: what, what for, what happens today, how often, and when | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Discovery question | Needs | A question for the people who do the work, answered in their words | same |
| System or account (asset) | Needs | A system, account, vendor, or data source the work touches. Never passwords | same |
| Requirement | Needs | Something the result must do, with a priority: must, should, or could | same |
| Option | Needs | One way to solve it, from neon1: cost, timeline, and scores for cost, quality, and effort (1 to 5, more is better), and whether neon1 recommends it | Draft, Proposed (shared for approval), Declined, Approved |
| Decision | Needs | The permanent record of an approved option, with the approver's signature | Approved (a record, can't change) |
| Constraint or assumption | Needs | Something the work depends on or is limited by, printed in the proposal | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Proposal revision | Needs | One issued, frozen revision of the project's proposal, such as 0039-r1. Made only by **Issue the proposal** | a record |
| File needed | Needs | A file neon1 asked the client for | Done once the file is sent |
| Task | Execute | One piece of work someone can finish | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Milestone | Execute | A point everyone can see, such as a launch | same |
| Change request | Execute | A change to what was agreed, with its effect on cost and dates | same |
| Hours | Execute | Time neon1 worked on one day, in quarter hours, with what it went to. Only neon1 adds entries; the client reads them | a record, kept as logged once an invoice bills it |
| Purchase | Execute | Something to buy for the approved option: estimate, actual cost, where it was bought, who buys it (the client or neon1), and its receipt | Open, Bought, Installed (done), Returned |
| Invoice | Execute | A bill for the work or for purchases, numbered when issued (such as INV-0039-01) | Draft, Issued, Paid, Void. Partly paid, bank payment clearing, and overdue are worked out from payments and the due date |
| Payment | Execute | Money received against one invoice, from Stripe or recorded by neon1 | a record |
| Status update | Execute | One line on how it's going, with a health; posting it sets the project's health | a record |
| Measure (metric) | Observe | A number that shows it worked: unit, baseline, target, which way is better, and dated readings | Done when it reaches its target |
| Check | Observe | Something to test before calling it done | To do, In progress, Blocked, Done |
| Incident | Observe | Something that broke: what people saw, when, and what fixed it | same |
| Handover step | Normalize | A step before it's fully the client's, such as admin access transferred | same |
| Runbook | Normalize | Written steps for a job that comes up again | same |
| Training | Normalize | Who learns what, and how | same |
| Care | Normalize | Ongoing care after launch | same |
| Retro | Normalize | What went well, or what to do differently | same |

An item's title opens its panel: status, owner, due date, details, and comments. Its box ticks it done. Counts show done out of total. A choice between options counts as one, done once one is approved. Updates, decisions, revisions, invoices, payments, and files aren't counted.

Who may do what with items:

- Anyone who can read the project (viewers too) may add a **request** and comment.
- Editors and admins add, edit, tick off, and delete other items.
- **Options** come only from neon1, which writes, shares (Proposed), and withdraws them. A client who wants another comments or adds a request.
- **Proposal revisions**, **invoices**, and **payments** come only from neon1, and once issued can't be edited or deleted.
- An **approved option** and its **decision** can't be edited or deleted. To change course, the decision maker approves a different option, and the earlier decision stays on record, marked as replaced (see **Changing the decision**).

## Options and the proposal

Options are compared on the Needs tab (`#options`), each with its cost (one-time and recurring apart, with a first-year total), timeline, three scores, and any Recommended mark. An option can also carry neon1's hours, costs paid to vendors, expected purchases (what, why, an example, an estimate, who buys it), and the result the client can check.

An option's price is one of two kinds, and the option says which:

- **Fixed** ("$6,500 fixed"): the whole price for the work described, changed only by an approved change.
- **Estimate** ("$3,500 to $4,200 estimate"): a range of hours at an hourly rate. The client pays for hours worked, each listed under Hours, never past the high end without an approved change. Fewer hours cost less.

Either way, **How this adds up** lists the work line by line with hours, the expected total, and **When you pay**: the deposit at approval and the rest at handover. Each option says why neon1 recommends it, or when to pick it. The proposal prints the same breakdown.

A project has one proposal, issued in numbered revisions. While neon1 shapes the options it's a **draft** the client can read but not approve. **Issue the proposal** freezes and numbers a copy: the first 1NEON issued is 0039, so its first revision is **0039-r1**. Each option gets the revision plus a letter, such as **0039-r1-B**, and the decision names that ID.

A later change of option, estimate, or scope is issued as the next revision, 0039-r2. Earlier ones stay readable, marked "Replaced by a later revision", and none can be edited or deleted.

**Read the proposal**, under the options, opens `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`: discovery, goals, constraints and assumptions, every shared option with what's in and out, a cost table, what each side will do, and the agreement. It shows the latest revision, with earlier ones a choice away. **Print or save as PDF** prints only the proposal, with its ID and page number on every page. **Download Word** saves `neon1-{org}-proposal-0039-r1.docx`, with the ID in the name, properties, and every header, so a marked-up copy uploaded to Files prompts "Is this a revision of Proposal 0039-r1?" and is filed with that revision.

### Price checks

Estimates are checked when a revision is issued and again after 30 days. Past that, approval waits until the decision maker chooses **Ask neon1 to refresh** and neon1 issues a revision with checked prices. Revisions don't otherwise expire.

### Changes of scope

A request added after approval asks "Does this change what was approved?" (**Yes, it changes it**, **No**, or **Not sure**). One marked as a change is flagged for, and answered in, the next revision.

## Approving and signing

**Approve this option** is offered only to the person allowed to approve on that project:

- the project's named **decision maker**, or several, any of whom may approve;
- if nobody is named, an **admin of the client organization**;
- never neon1, which proposed the options, except in neon1's own organization (N1-0001), where neon1 is the client.

Neo never approves for anyone. Asked to, it points to **Approve this option**.

Approving needs all of these, and 1NEON says which is missing:

1. neon1 has issued the proposal, and the option is in the latest revision.
2. The option hasn't changed since that revision was issued.
3. The revision is within its price check.
4. An admin of the client organization has signed neon1's [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md) at its current edition. (Not needed in N1-0001.)

Approving restates exactly what's accepted: the option and its ID, its proposal, estimate, timeline, neon1's hours, vendor costs, purchases, and the result to check. The approver may add conditions ("only after 6pm"), then types their full name and ticks the consent box: "I agree to sign electronically. My typed name is my signature, and I can ask neon1 for a paper copy at any time."

The decision records the option ID, the approver's name and email, the time, the option's version, its terms exactly as shown, and the signature: typed name, consent, a SHA-256 fingerprint of the signed terms, and the address and browser. If the option changed after it was opened, the approval is refused for review. A signed approval records that the organization agreed to that option's scope, cost, and timeline, as on paper. The printed and Word proposals show it.

Approving also:

- The option's expected purchases join Execute, marked with its ID.
- Drafts a deposit invoice for neon1 to check and issue, when the price is in numbers: half a fixed price, or half an estimate's low end. Nothing reaches the client until it's issued.

Only a client admin, after confirming it's them, can name or change the decision maker, under People on the Overview; editors change everyone else. neon1 can't be decision maker outside its own organization.

### Changing the decision

Until the handover is accepted, the decision maker can choose a different option with **Choose this instead**. The screen says **Change to 0039-r1-C?** and adds what the change replaces (the option, when it was approved, and by whom), what was already invoiced for it, the hours already logged, and the deposit asked now. A reason is required, and the change is signed like an approval; the reason and the replaced decision go into the signed fingerprint.

- Nothing is billed twice. Money invoiced for the replaced decision counts toward the new one, so its deposit asks only for the difference, or nothing. An unissued deposit draft for the replaced decision is removed, and the new option's takes its place.
- Hours already logged count toward the new option's hours, and its high end still caps the total.
- If what was invoiced comes to more than the new option can cost, accepting the handover drafts a credit for the difference.
- The replaced decision stays in Needs, marked "replaced by a later decision", and its option shows **replaced**. The new decision shows **Why it changed**.
- Going back to a replaced option waits until neon1 confirms it in the next revision, with checked prices; then it shows **Go back to this option**.
- Once the handover is accepted, the decision stays. Everyone following Decisions and options is told of a change, and the activity record says from what, to what, and why.

## The service agreement

neon1's service agreement covers every project with an organization. Anyone can read it at `/1NEON/agreement`. A client admin signs it once at `/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement`, from **Settings** or the notice under the options, with a typed name and the consent box, before the first approval. The signature records the edition (now 2.0, which added how estimates are billed and that a deposit counts toward the final invoice), a SHA-256 fingerprint of its text, the time, and where it came from. A new edition is signed again before the next approval, and an earlier signature keeps the text it was given. The full text is in the [service agreement](../engagement/service-agreement.md).

## Purchases

**Purchases**, in Execute, start from the approved option's expected purchases. Each shows its estimate, the actual cost and where, who buys it, and its receipt; a bought item without one is flagged. Statuses are **Open**, **Bought**, **Installed** (done), and **Returned**.

- **The client buys it** ("You buy it."): in the organization's name, keeping the receipt with the project (**Attach the receipt**).
- **neon1 buys it**: only after the decision maker initials that neon1 buys it and is paid back at cost, in the signed approval or later on the purchase. Until then it says "Waiting on the decision maker's initials before neon1 buys it." neon1 attaches the receipt and bills exactly that amount, with no markup.

## Handover acceptance

Handover steps in Normalize are ticked as they're done, by either side. Until all are, the steps say how many are left; then the decision maker sees "Every step is done" and chooses **Accept the handover**, with an optional note ("What you checked") and **Sign and accept the handover**, signed like an approval. One signature accepts every remaining step, each keeping its own record with "Accepted by", name, and date. **Check it and accept** accepts a single unticked step and marks it done. An accepted step can't be unticked. Acceptance drafts a final invoice for neon1: what's left on a fixed price, or the hours worked less earlier invoices on an estimate. Home's **Needs you** and the project's **Next step** prompt the decision maker when it's time.

## Hours

Hours are in Execute under **Hours** (`#hours`). neon1 logs each entry's date, quarter hours, and what it went to. The client reads them only. On an estimate, the section shows hours against the range, their cost at the rate, and a bar to the high end with a mark at the low end. Hours past the high end are listed, not billed. On a fixed price, hours are a record, not a bill.

Issuing a progress or final invoice on an estimate marks unbilled hours with its number ("billed on INV-0039-02"). Those entries then stay as logged, and a mistake is corrected with a credit.

## Invoices and paying

Invoices are in Execute (`#billing`). neon1 makes them, and the client sees them only once issued.

| Type | When it comes up |
|---|---|
| Deposit | Drafted when an option with a price in numbers is approved: half of a fixed price, or half of an estimate's low end |
| Progress | Added by neon1 for a stage of the work. On an estimate: the hours worked so far, less earlier invoices |
| Final | Drafted when the last handover step is accepted: what's left on a fixed price, or the hours worked (never past the high end) less earlier invoices |
| Purchases at cost | Reimbursement for what neon1 bought, from the receipts |
| Care plan | The monthly fee for ongoing care |
| Credit | Reduces an issued invoice it names |

**New invoice** (neon1) picks a type, and empty lines fill from the approved option or receipts. **Save draft** keeps it private. **Issue** numbers it (**INV-0039-01**: the proposal's number, or the project key, and its place in the project), sets a due date (15 days by default), addresses it to the decision maker or a client admin, fixes its contents with a SHA-256 fingerprint, and tells the client by bell and email.

Each invoice has its own page, `/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`: from, bill to, lines, sales tax, total, credits, payments, balance due, terms, and how to pay, ready to print or save as a PDF. An invoice for hours lists the entries it covers and names the earlier invoices it subtracts. If the work comes to less than a deposit paid, neon1 refunds the difference as a credit. An invoice reads as **Draft**, **Open**, **Partly paid**, **Overdue** (past its due date with a balance), **Paid in full**, **Void**, or **Credit**.

Paying:

- **Online:** **See and pay**, then **Pay**, opens Stripe Checkout for the balance, bank transfer (ACH) first and card too. 1NEON never sees card or bank details. A card payment shows as paid at once. A bank payment shows as **bank payment clearing**, with its amount and date, until the bank clears it in a few business days; meanwhile **Pay** is gone and nothing counts it overdue or asks for it, so nobody pays twice. If the bank refuses it, no money moved: the invoice reopens with the failed payment listed and **Pay again**, and Next step and Needs you say so. Billing contacts are told when a bank payment starts, clears, or fails.
- **By check, Zelle, or wire:** neon1 records it with **Record a payment** when it arrives: the amount, how it arrived, the date, and a check number or confirmation.
- No surcharge is added for any way of paying.

Issued invoices and payments are permanent. A mistake is fixed with a **credit** or by voiding with a reason (**Void invoice**), both kept on record. An invoice with payments, or one clearing, is credited rather than voided; one whose only payment failed can be voided. Every signature, issued invoice, and payment is also kept write-protected for seven years.

The **Agreements, invoices, and payments** notification group (email on by default) covers the agreement signed, invoices issued or voided, and payments started, arrived, or failed. Drafts never reach the client.

## Next step

**Next step**, at the top of every project, shows the one thing to do now and who it waits on, the first of these that applies:

1. For client members, an invoice with something to pay: "Invoice INV-0039-01 is ready" (or **overdue**, or "The bank payment on invoice INV-0039-01 didn't go through"), the amount, and the due date, with **See and pay**. An invoice covered by a bank payment that's clearing isn't listed.
2. For neon1, invoice drafts: "A deposit invoice is drafted. Check it, then issue.", with **Check invoices**.
3. For neon1, shared options not yet in an issued revision: "Issue the proposal so the client can approve an option" (or its next revision, such as r2), with **Issue the proposal** or **Issue r2**.
4. Options are shared and you may approve: "Choose an option: {n} ready for your approval in Proposal 0039-r1", or that the estimates are due a price check, or that neon1 is preparing the proposal, with **Compare options**.
5. Options are shared and someone else approves: "Waiting on {decision maker} to choose an option", with **See options**.
6. Files are asked for (for client members): "Send {n} files", with **Upload**.
7. Every handover step is done and you may accept: "Every handover step is done. Check them, then accept the handover with one signature.", with **Review and accept**.
8. You have open items assigned to you: "You have {n} open items here", with **Open**.
9. An option is approved and the project is at or before Decide: "{option} is approved. Next, move the project to {next stage}", with **Move to** for neon1. A client reads "Next, neon1 moves the project to {next stage}".
10. For neon1: "Add options" when none exist yet near Decide, or "Share an option" when options exist but none is shared.
11. Otherwise the stage's goal. neon1 reads "To finish {stage}: {done when}", with **Move to {next stage}** (not past Decide without an approval). A client reads who has the work: "{stage} is with neon1. It's done when: {done when}. Then neon1 moves the project to {next stage}. Nothing needs you right now." In neon1's own organization, editors get the move as neon1 does.
12. "Nothing needs doing right now."

## Health

Health is **Not assessed** (the start), **On track**, **At risk**, or **Off track**. Only people change it, on the Overview or by posting a status update ("How is it going?"), which records who and when.

## Starting a project

**New project** (editors and admins) asks for a template, a name, what it is, what will be true when it's done, one real example of today's work, a target date, any sensitive data (PII, PHI, or payment), and optional measures with baseline and target. Templates start it with fitting items:

| Template | Key | Starts with |
|---|---|---|
| Blank | PRJ | Nothing |
| Cloud migration | MIG | Discovery questions, servers and files assets, a must-have requirement, cost and downtime measures, a backup restore check, and the handover checklist |
| Workflow automation | FLOW | Discovery questions, tools and inboxes asset, "nothing is retyped twice", turnaround and staff-time measures, and the handover checklist |
| Networks and connected systems | NET | Discovery questions, sites, devices, and connections asset, "guest and device traffic can't reach business systems", an unplanned-outages measure, a failover or restore check, and the handover checklist |
| AI assistant | AI | Discovery questions, document sources asset, "answers cite their source", time-to-answer and correctness measures, and the handover checklist |
| Security readiness | SEC | Discovery questions, systems in scope, "MFA on every admin account", an open-findings measure, an access review check, and the handover checklist |
| Personal or home tech | HOME | "What's not working, in your own words", devices and accounts involved, and "Written steps left behind" |

Every template except Blank and Personal or home tech starts with this handover checklist:

- Accounts are in the client's name.
- Admin access is transferred to the client.
- Docs are delivered and walked through.
- The people who use it are trained on it.
- Older tools are retired or merged.
- neon1's access is reduced or removed.

## The Overview tab

Overview shows any decision, the summary and outcome, measures with progress, a side column (health and who set it, stage and dates, the latest update, sensitive-data flags, people, and **Archive this project**), **How is it going?**, and **People on this project** with roles: lead engineer, sponsor, decision maker, tech contact, stakeholder, and observer. Roles describe work and never grant access, except that a decision maker may approve.

docs.text:
# 1NEON guide: every page, what it shows, and who can do what

Each signed-in 1NEON page: what it's for, what's on it, its states, and the actions on it with the access each one needs.

Access levels build up. **Viewers** read, comment, add requests, and approve when they're a project's decision maker. **Editors** also add and change work. **Admins** also invite people, change access and settings, and delete projects, files, and others' comments, after a recent "confirm it's you". neon1 acts as an admin everywhere but never approves for a client.

## Home

`/1NEON/o/{org}/workspace`.

- **Needs you** lists what's waiting on you, most pressing first, each with its action: **See and pay** (an invoice due, overdue, or whose bank payment failed, but not one clearing), **Compare options**, **Review and accept** (a finished handover), **Upload file**, or **Open**. neon1 sees invoice drafts with **Check it**. Empty, it says "You're all caught up".
- **Coming up** shows three weeks as a strip of days marked with due dates, milestones, and targets, then the next six weeks listed by Overdue, This week, Next week, and Later.
- **Get started** is a setup checklist that disappears once done: the tour, a first project (editors), inviting the team, and a second step for admin actions (admins).
- **Recent activity**: what people did lately, newest first.
- **Your free account**, in a free account only: the date it's deleted if nothing changes, **Keep it 30 more days** (once), and **Download a copy** (Settings, Your data).
- **Next step**, in a free account only: **Ask for an assessment** or **Ask for a call**, with an optional note. Each emails neon1, and the reply comes by email. The assessment is free: neon1's written read of the project as written, with a likely approach and the first questions to settle. neon1 reads it before the 15-minute call, which is about needs.

## Board

`/1NEON/o/{org}/workflow`. Every project as a card in its stage. Editors and admins drag cards, or use **Move to** on a phone; passing Decide without an approval asks for a reason. Columns show "Done when", the count, and any limit.

## Projects

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects`. All projects, as a **List** (stage, health, target date; filter by layer; sort by stage, target date, or recent changes) or a **Timeline** (each project drawn from its start to its target date, colored by layer; the dashed line is today, the diamond the target, red stripes time past the target, and each row says its stage and days left). **New project** starts one (editors and admins).

## New project

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/new`. Editors and admins pick a template, name and describe it, give its outcome and one real example, and optionally a target date, sensitive-data flags, and measures.

## One project

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}`, with tabs Overview, Needs, Execute, Observe, and Normalize (`/needs`, `/execute`, `/observe`, `/normalize`). The header shows the key, stage and time in it, name, health, and the onion, under **Next step**. Details are in the projects guide. Actions:

| Action | Who |
|---|---|
| Read, comment on items | Everyone in the organization |
| Add a request | Everyone, viewers too |
| Add, edit, tick off, or delete tasks, questions, measures, checks, and other items | Editors and admins |
| Edit name, summary, outcome, target date; set health; post a status update; move stage; archive | Editors and admins |
| Change people on the project (not the decision maker) | Editors and admins |
| Name or change the decision maker | Admins of the client, after confirming it's them (in N1-0001 also neon1) |
| Approve an option, with a typed signature | The named decision maker; with none named, a client admin. Only from an issued revision, within its price check, once the service agreement is signed |
| Ask neon1 to refresh a revision past its price check | Whoever may approve |
| Initial a purchase neon1 buys; check and accept a handover step | Whoever may approve |
| Add, share, or withdraw options; issue the proposal or its next revision | neon1 only |
| Add a purchase, attach a receipt, mark it bought, installed, or returned | Editors and admins (neon1 marks its own purchases bought only after the decision maker's initials) |
| Read issued invoices; pay one online | Everyone in the client organization |
| Draft, issue, void, or credit an invoice; record a check, Zelle, or wire payment | neon1 only |
| Move to Trash | Admins, after confirming it's them, typing the project's key |

Files asked for show under Needs with **Upload**, and measures take dated readings. Someone else editing shows as a small avatar beside the name.

## The proposal

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/proposal`. The proposal on neon1's letterhead, for everyone in the organization: the latest revision (such as 0039-r2), or the draft before the first, with earlier ones marked as replaced and any signed approval shown. **Print or save as PDF** and **Download Word** keep a copy.

## An invoice

`/1NEON/o/{org}/projects/{KEY}/invoices/{id}`. One invoice on neon1's letterhead, ready to print or save as a PDF: its number, dates, bill to, lines, tax, total, credits, payments, the balance due, the terms, and how to pay. **Back to invoices** returns to the project's Invoices. A draft says "Draft, only neon1 sees it. Issuing numbers it and shows it to the client."

## The service agreement

`/1NEON/o/{org}/agreement` (signed in) and `/1NEON/agreement` (public). The agreement, its edition, and **Signatures**: who signed which edition and when. A client admin signs it once with a typed name and the consent box.

## One layer across projects

`/1NEON/o/{org}/layer/{needs|execute|observe|normalize}`. One layer's items across every project. Open a project to change them.

## People

`/1NEON/o/{org}/people`. Who's in the organization, their title, access, and status.

- **Invite people** (admins): up to 50 emails at once, with an access level and optional names and titles. Each gets an email link and signs in with a code.
- Each invitation shows whether its email went out: queued, sent, or failed. **Resend** sends it again (rate limited).
- Admins change access or titles, or **deactivate** someone, ending their access until reactivated.
- Member statuses: **Invited** (hasn't signed in yet), **Joined**, **Deactivated**.
- neon1's own access shows without a way to change it.

## Files

`/1NEON/o/{org}/documents`. Every file in the organization. Anyone, viewers too, can **Upload** up to 100 MB, to a project or none. Files move through **Receiving**, **Checking** (virus and size), **Ready**, **Rejected** (a threat found), or **Failed** (missing, wrong size, or the scan didn't finish). PDFs, pictures, and text open in a tab; others download. Uploaders and admins can delete. No passwords, keys, or regulated data without an agreement that covers it.

## Insights

`/1NEON/o/{org}/insights`. Charts from the organization's data: open and overdue work, the on-time rate, days to a decision, measures at target, items finished per week for eight weeks, projects by layer, and health. Work counts as finished the day it was marked done.

## Settings

`/1NEON/o/{org}/settings`. **Where**: the organization's website or public page and where it's based (a city and state, a state alone, or a place outside the US), checked the same way as on sign-up; any admin can **Change** it without confirming it's them, and Home asks the organization's admins for it until one is added or they choose **Not now**. Both are optional. The service agreement's signer and edition, or "not signed yet", with **Read and sign**. Then the board's stages, each with name, layer, "Done when", optional limit, **Show** or **Hide**, and order. **Save workflow** saves all (admins, after confirming it's them). A stage holding projects can't be removed.

## Your profile

`/1NEON/me`. Name, title, phone (only you see it), theme (Matrix: Awake or Plugged; Sentinel: Providence or Desert of the real; or Match my device), menu (Default or Mini), and **Notifications**: for each group (files; people and access; decisions and options; agreements, invoices, and payments; workflow and stages; comments; updates and items; sign-ins) whether it reaches you by email, by text, or neither. Then **Save**. Also here: texts (add a mobile number, agree to texts, confirm the code), **Two-step verification** at `#security` (passkey, authenticator app, text-message codes), **Replay the tutorial**, and **Sign out**. Two-step changes and signing out take effect at once.

## Contact

`/1NEON/contact`. **Contact neon1**, in the menu for every account, free accounts included: email hello@neon1.tech, call or text (424) 32-neon1, or book a free 15-minute call, with the hours I answer. Anything about a project is best written in that project.

## All clients

`/1NEON/all/workflow`, neon1 only. Every client's projects on one read-only board, **By organization** (each organization with its client ID, such as N1-0001, and how many projects are active) or **One board**. To change anything, open the client.

## Public pages

The sign-in screen (`/1NEON/`), FAQs, service agreement, sample project, guided walkthrough, interactive demo, and policies need no account. Neo on the sign-in screen is the public Neo, which only knows neon1's public pages.
